newsitem.title: CHINA: China economists see high growth, low inflation.
newsitem.headline: China economists see high growth, low inflation.

text.p: China is set to enter a period of high growth and low inflation if it maintains current macroeconomic policy and speeds up reform of its lumbering state sector, the China Daily said on Wednesday.

"This is the key to ensuring long-term stable economic growth," it quoted a report by the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences Economic Institute, the Unirule Institute of Economics and Development and the Hong Kong and Macau International Trust and Investment Co Research Centre as saying.

Beijing should take advantage of the current favourable economic climate to deepen reform of its economic system, speeding up acquisitions and mergers of enterprises and improving liquidity of state assets through property sales, the report said.

"With the establishment of the money policy committee of the People's Bank of China, China's macroeconomic policies are more operational and China is expected to enter a new economic growth stage with no inflation," the report said.
However, the economists dismissed reports that while China's macroeconomy was healthy, its microeconomy was deteriorating, with rising losses among enterprises.
"The macroeconomy is not as good as the statistics indicate and enterprises are not as bad as the statistics indicate," they said.
China's economy grew at a rate of 9.5 percent in the first half of this year with retail inflation at 1.8 percent year-on-year. Inflation was 6.1 percent in 1996.
Officials have forecast economic growth will be about 10 percent this year with inflation around four percent.
